summary.name: Wysa
summary.one_liner: Wysa is an AI mental health and wellbeing support service offering anonymous self-help, guided referral, and between-session care for individuals, employers, and health systems.
use_cases: Venting or talking through negative thoughts and emotions
Self-help coping tools between therapy sessions
Primary care integrated behavioral health via CoCM
Employer or health system wellbeing support
Support for adolescents in low-resource settings
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Wysa as an anonymous, AI-powered mental health support service that is always available with no appointments. It offers self-help, guided referral, and between-session care, with human oversight in all care pathways. Wysa says its AI does not make decisions on its own and that it cannot give medical or clinical advice. Through a partnership with April Health, it supports the Collaborative Care Model in primary care, and through Kins it links AI support with licensed physical therapy. The page cites peer-reviewed research, a claimed user base of over 6 million people, and deployments such as mindline.sg in Singapore.
notable: Human oversight built into all care pathways, with AI that does not make decisions on its own
Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) support through April Health partnership
Physical and mental health bridge via Kins (licensed physical therapy)
Backed by peer-reviewed studies and deployments by health systems and governments
caveats: Not designed for crises, abuse, suicidal feelings, self-harm, or medical emergencies; users are directed to hotlines and professional help
Users must be at least 18, or 13 to 18 with parent or guardian review of terms; not for children under 13
Pricing details are not given on the page; the freemium label comes from the directory listing only
